## MARKET OVERVIEW

**1. What is the Current Market Regime?**
RISK-ON: normal volatility at 33.0% and strong breadth, with 7/8 sectors positive. Participation is broad, though the positive breadth sits alongside substantial weakness in several stocks on a one-month view.

**2. Which sectors are leading?**
Transportation leads (1W: +6.44% | 1M: +15.28%), ABOVE TREND; its standout is PGSUS (1W: +9.68% | 1M: +19.74%), ABOVE TREND. Construction & REIT (1W: +3.99% | 1M: -2.74%) and Heavy Industry (1W: +3.14% | 1M: -7.44%) are in RECOVERY; ALARK (1W: +7.17% | 1M: +0.74%) is ABOVE TREND.

**3. Which sectors are lagging?**
Holding & Investment is the only negative sector on the week (1W: -2.70% | 1M: -2.64%), BELOW TREND; SAHOL (1W: -2.41% | 1M: +0.53%) is in CORRECTION. Retail & Food is barely positive on the week but negative over the month (1W: +0.11% | 1M: -7.51%), in RECOVERY.

## STOCK PERFORMANCE

**4. Top Performing Stocks?**
PGSUS (1W: +9.68% | 1M: +19.74%), ABOVE TREND; CCOLA (1W: +9.62% | 1M: -0.93%), RECOVERY; TCELL (1W: +7.78% | 1M: -1.32%), RECOVERY. KRDMD (1W: +7.58% | 1M: -9.87%) is in RECOVERY, while ALARK (1W: +7.17% | 1M: +0.74%) is ABOVE TREND.

**5. Worst Performing Stocks?**
TRMET (1W: -0.98% | 1M: -14.31%), BELOW TREND; GUBRF (1W: -1.64% | 1M: -27.24%), BELOW TREND; AEFES (1W: -1.78% | 1M: -9.27%), BELOW TREND. SAHOL (1W: -2.41% | 1M: +0.53%) is in CORRECTION, and ARCLK (1W: -2.92% | 1M: -11.04%) is BELOW TREND.

**6. Momentum Stocks?**
The strongest weekly advances came from PGSUS (1W: +9.68% | 1M: +19.74%), ABOVE TREND; CCOLA (1W: +9.62% | 1M: -0.93%), RECOVERY; and TCELL (1W: +7.78% | 1M: -1.32%), RECOVERY. KRDMD (1W: +7.58% | 1M: -9.87%) and VESTL (1W: +7.11% | 1M: -18.30%) also bounced, both in RECOVERY.

## SECTOR OUTLOOK

**7. Banking Sector Outlook?**
Banking & Finance is ABOVE TREND (1W: +2.07% | 1M: +4.29%); GARAN (1W: +4.16% | 1M: +15.17%) leads the available bank data, ABOVE TREND. AKBNK (1W: +1.89% | 1M: +4.25%), ISCTR (1W: +1.96% | 1M: +4.15%) and YKBNK (1W: +1.45% | 1M: +5.12%) are also ABOVE TREND.

**8. Industrial Sector Outlook?**
Heavy Industry remains in RECOVERY on sector averages (1W: +3.14% | 1M: -7.44%); EREGL (1W: +5.28% | 1M: -11.86%) is in RECOVERY. FROTO (1W: +0.82% | 1M: +2.64%) is ABOVE TREND, while ASELS (1W: +4.14% | 1M: -0.72%) is in RECOVERY.

**9. Energy & Chemicals Outlook?**
Energy & Chemicals is in RECOVERY on sector averages (1W: +0.80% | 1M: -13.35%), with sharp divergence beneath the surface. TUPRS (1W: +6.37% | 1M: -8.18%) and SISE (1W: +4.73% | 1M: -4.17%) are in RECOVERY, while HEKTS (1W: -4.55% | 1M: -20.38%) is BELOW TREND.

## PORTFOLIO STRATEGY

**10. Portfolio Recommendation?**
Maintain a constructive but selective stance: RISK-ON conditions and broad participation favor measured exposure, especially to sectors with positive one-month momentum. Keep risk controls tight and avoid treating weekly rebounds as confirmed reversals where the one-month trend remains negative.

## NEXT WEEK OUTLOOK

**11. Stocks to Watch Next Week?**
Track PGSUS (1W: +9.68% | 1M: +19.74%), ABOVE TREND, and THYAO (1W: +7.02% | 1M: +14.68%), ABOVE TREND, for continuation. GARAN (1W: +4.16% | 1M: +15.17%), ABOVE TREND, is a banking leader; TUPRS (1W: +6.37% | 1M: -8.18%), RECOVERY, is a test of whether the bounce can extend.

**12. Sectors to Watch Next Week?**
Monitor Transportation, the strongest sector on both weekly and monthly returns, and Banking & Finance, where sector momentum and available bank trends are positive. Watch Heavy Industry for confirmation that its weekly recovery can improve the still-negative monthly picture.

**13. Key Levels & Triggers?**
Specific XU100 support and resistance levels were not provided; avoid assigning numerical levels from this dataset. Watch for breadth slipping below 5/8 positive sectors or 20-day volatility rising above 40% as triggers for a less favorable regime.

## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The market is RISK-ON, supported by normal volatility and 7/8 positive sector breadth, with Transportation and Banking & Finance leading. Strong weekly rebounds are widespread, but negative one-month sector averages in Heavy Industry and Energy & Chemicals—and continued weakness in select stocks—argue for selectivity and disciplined risk limits.
